name: Eitrigg
summary: In Orgrimmar, Eitrigg stands beside Warchief Thrall as a trusted advisor. A veteran of the First and Second Wars, he left the Blackrock clan’s Horde after its defeat and lived in exile. Now he helps Thrall guide the New Horde toward honor and shamanism.

sections.title: A Veteran of the Old Horde
sections.body: Born on Draenor among the Blackrock clan, Eitrigg fought for the Horde in the First and Second Wars. The battles and the Horde’s defeat in the second war forced him to face how far his people had fallen into bloodlust and demonic corruption. Sickened by what the Horde had become, he left its scattered remnants and sought solitude in the wilds of Lordaeron.

sections.title: Blood and Honor
sections.body: During his exile, Eitrigg sheltered in an abandoned tower near Hearthglen. The human paladin Tirion Fordring found him, and their clash brought the tower’s ruins down around them. Eitrigg pulled the unconscious human to safety instead of finishing him. Moved by this act of martial honor, Tirion swore friendship and kept the hermit’s location secret. The local Alliance authorities eventually captured Eitrigg and sentenced him to hang in Stratholme. Tirion cast aside his knighthood, lands, and freedom to attack the city and rescue him. Their bond showed both warriors that honor could cross the hatred between their peoples.

sections.title: Counselor to the Warchief
sections.body: In Stratholme, Thrall’s newly united Horde raided the city during Tirion’s attempt to free Eitrigg and carried the aging warrior away. Meeting Thrall convinced Eitrigg that the orcs were casting off demonic corruption and returning to their ancestral shamanic heritage. He crossed the Great Sea with Thrall to Kalimdor and took a revered place in Orgrimmar’s Valley of Wisdom. Now Eitrigg advises the young Warchief inside Grommash Hold. He helps evaluate new recruits and shares the wisdom he earned, so the New Horde does not repeat the tragedies of the past.

faq.answer: Eitrigg is an elderly Blackrock orc warrior and veteran of the First and Second Wars. He now resides in Grommash Hold in Orgrimmar, advising Warchief Thrall.

faq.q: Why does Eitrigg consider a human his brother?
faq.answer: In exile in Lordaeron, Eitrigg saved the paladin Tirion Fordring when their duel brought down a stone tower. Tirion kept Eitrigg’s location secret and later fought his own people in Stratholme to prevent his execution, giving up his title and lands. Their shared honor made them brothers.

faq.q: What clan does Eitrigg belong to?
faq.answer: Eitrigg belongs to the Blackrock clan. He fought in the old wars, then abandoned the Horde’s corrupt remnants after seeing their demonic corruption.

faq.q: Why did Eitrigg leave the old Horde?
faq.answer: After the Horde’s defeat in the Second War, Eitrigg saw that bloodlust and demonic corruption had stripped his people of honor. He left in disgust, seeking a quiet place to die rather than serve a corrupt war machine.

faq.q: How did Eitrigg end up in Orgrimmar?
faq.answer: When Alliance forces captured Eitrigg and prepared to execute him in Stratholme, Thrall’s forces raided the city and freed him. Eitrigg saw Thrall’s commitment to honor and the return to shamanism, then chose to follow him to Kalimdor.

faq.q: What role does Eitrigg play in Orgrimmar right now?
faq.answer: In Grommash Hold, Eitrigg advises Thrall and helps test and evaluate recruits who swear loyalty to the New Horde.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you can look to Eitrigg as its living memory. He stands beside Thrall to help keep the mistakes of the demon-tainted past from being repeated.
As a warrior, you can see in Eitrigg martial honor preserved through decades of tragedy. He survived two wars through strength and unbroken discipline.
As a paladin, you know the story of Eitrigg and Tirion Fordring as a renowned test of duty and righteous honor.
As an orc of Durotar, you can look to Eitrigg as a revered elder. His Blackrock heritage shows that any orc can embrace honor and redeem their people’s legacy.
